findings.text: _review_single_batch selects the same registry conventions the node guarded at three sites, calling conventions_context_for(item.get('standard_name') or item['id']) with no try/except, so an unparseable id still raises ParseError and aborts that docs-review batch exactly as it did before the fix; the node was fenced to workers.py so the repair is out of scope, and it did not name this site in its manifest (the brief asked that a cause in review/pipeline.py be named). test_conventions_wiring.py:190 drives this site only with a parseable name, so no test reddens on it.

item_verdicts.call_sites: the helper is reached by three production render sites, imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:9658 (process_generate_docs_batch), :10334 (prepare_docs_review_request) and :10696 (process_refine_docs_batch); a fourth production site that selects the same conventions, imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:2042 (_review_single_batch), was not routed through it and stays unguarded.
item_verdicts.diff: read 30da80473 (workers.py +17/-6, three goldens) and 0c97c1049 (fragment +68) against base 3035a198 commit by commit; workers.py adds one helper and replaces three direct conventions_context_for calls, and the three goldens are recaptured by rendering (run-dir helper capture_goldens.py:33 renders each template with a no-edit context and writes it), never hand-edited.
item_verdicts.done_when: the done_when asks that each test passes at head via a product fix or a golden update stated per test, and that the prompt/review/pool gate add no failure against base with baseline_suite and after_suite recorded; both suite arms are completed true (logs/baseline_suite.log 33 failed/1891 passed, logs/after_suite.log 21 failed/1916 passed) and the after ids minus the base ids is the empty set, so zero are added.

justifications.durability: the existing six tests are the guard and the negative control demonstrates them: restoring the pre-repair content of the four files (logs/negative_control.log) reddens all six with EXIT=1, so the suite fails if this fix regresses.
justifications.evidence: the gate the worker ran is the prompt/review/pool file set over the six, with the delta measured from recorded arms (logs/baseline_suite.log 33 failed/1891 passed at 776b372e6 versus logs/after_suite.log 21 failed/1916 passed at head), giving 0 added ids; the base arm is a revision older than the node's parent 3035a198, so the delta is conservative and could not hide a failure the node introduced that is absent at 776b372e6.
justifications.fit: the helper at imas_codex/standard_names/workers.py:9501 uses the same try/except-Exception-degrade idiom as the neighbouring scored-example load at workers.py:9610, is named by mechanism, and carries no plan or ticket label.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the goal is the six passing at head, and logs/head_six_after.log:6 records '6 passed' EXIT=0 at the reviewed head while logs/negative_control.log:24 records the same six red with EXIT=1 when the repaired files are reverted.
justifications.reuse: it wraps the owner of conventions selection, imas_codex/standard_names/context.py:28 conventions_context_for, rather than re-implementing select_conventions, but placing the degrade in a worker-local helper leaves the sibling production site at imas_codex/standard_names/review/pipeline.py:2042 outside the guard, which a degrade in the owner would have covered.
justifications.scope_discipline: every path in the two commits is inside the manifest's declared write paths, and the four test files and two prompt templates that were in scope are correctly left untouched.
